rio.normal.detalhe: On half of the days at this time of year, from {ini} to {fim}, the river had between {p25} and {p75} m³/s.
rio.normal.seca: A very low river can make boat transport, fishing and access to water harder.
rio.normal.cheia: River very high for the time of year: watch for flood warnings.
rio.normal.semHistorico: The comparison with previous years is not available yet.
rio.baldes: Today about {hoje} buckets of water per second flow through this stretch of the river.
rio.baldes.normal: In a normal season, it would be about {normal}.
rio.incerteza: The further away the date, the less certain the forecast. The blue band shows where the river should be in most scenarios.
rio.extremos: In the GloFAS model series for this stretch (since {ano}), the highest calculated value was {max} m³/s ({dataMax}) and the lowest was {min} m³/s ({dataMin}). These are model values, not measurements: the largest floods and droughts officially recorded come from ANA's stations.
rio.aviso: This is a computer model forecast (GloFAS) for the stretch of the {rio} near the city. It is not the measurement of the river gauge.
rio.unidade: m³/s = cubic meters of water flowing per second. 1 m³ = 1,000 liters = 50 buckets.

rio.normal.metodo: How we calculate normal: GloFAS model series from {ini} to {fim}. In each year, we use the {janela} days before and the {janela} days after {data} ({amostras} days in total).

ra.regua.descricao: River gauge with today's level ({hoje}), the reference levels and the marks of the largest flood and the largest drought.
ra.regua.legenda: Drawing to scale: the little figure is 1.60 m tall. The floor of the stilt house was drawn at the flood Emergency level, to show when water would get inside the house. At the bottom, in yellow, orange and red, the drought band. The numbers are from the {estacao} station gauge (level in meters, with the gauge's local reference; it is not the depth of the river).
ra.comparacao.titulo: Do the measurement and the model agree?
ra.comparacao.divergem: The measurement and the model disagree. ANA's measurement, taken in the river, is what counts.
ra.comparacao.concordam: The measurement and the model agree.
ra.comparacao.semNormal: The comparison with previous years appears when ANA's history finishes downloading.

ra.grafico.descricao: Chart of the river level over the last 7 days, with the reference level lines.

ra.historico.hoje: Today the river is {dif} below the largest flood recorded at this station.
ra.historico.reguasDiferentes: Each station has its own gauge: the numbers of one cannot be compared directly with the other's.

motivo.SUBIDA_RAPIDA_PREVISTA: {fonte}: forecast of a fast river rise ({variacao}% in 7 days).
inicio.titulo: How the community is right now
inicio.semRisco: No sign of flood or drought risk right now.
inicio.simulacao: SIMULATION: this level comes from the simulated sensor, used for demonstration. It is not a real measurement.
inicio.cotasProvisorias: The levels used are provisional, calculated from ANA's history (there is no official level for this station).
inicio.fontes: Sources: ANA measurement, community sensor (simulated), weather forecast (Open-Meteo) and GloFAS model.
inicio.verMapa: See safe points on the map
inicio.mochilaIntro: Keep it ready, in a high place that is easy to grab:
inicio.indisponivel: It was not possible to check the risk right now. Try again in a few minutes.
inicio.marcar: Check what you have already done:
seguro.NORMAL: Yes. There is no flood or drought risk right now.
seguro.CHEIA.ATENCAO: Yes, but stay alert: the river is high.
seguro.CHEIA.ALERTA: Get ready: you may need to leave home.
seguro.CHEIA.EMERGENCIA: No. Go now to a safe, high place.
seguro.SECA.ATENCAO: Yes, but the river is low for the time of year: take care of your water.
seguro.SECA.ALERTA: Careful: strong drought. Save water and treat it.
seguro.SECA.EMERGENCIA: Very serious drought. Go to Civil Defense to receive water and food.
legenda.NORMAL: All calm. Go on with normal life.
legenda.ALERTA: High risk. Get ready to act.
acoes.NORMAL: Follow the warnings on the radio, on your phone or from Civil Defense.
Agree with your family where to go if the river changes.
acoes.CHEIA.ATENCAO: Keep documents and medicines in a plastic bag, in a high place.
Move furniture, food and appliances up high.
Find the nearest safe point on the map and the way there.
Keep the canoe or boat ready and well tied.
Watch the warnings: the river may rise more.
acoes.CHEIA.ALERTA: Get ready to leave home: take the emergency bag.
Take children, elderly people, people with disabilities and sick people first.
Turn off the power at the meter if water gets close to the outlets.
Do not let children play in flood water.
Warn neighbors who do not have a phone.
acoes.CHEIA.EMERGENCIA: Leave now for a safe, high place.
Turn off power and gas before leaving, if there is time.
Do not cross moving water, on foot or in a small canoe.
If someone is in danger, call 193 (Fire Department) or 199 (Civil Defense).
Help those in need, without putting yourself at risk.
acoes.SECA.ATENCAO: Drinking water: store clean water in covered containers.
Boil or filter water before drinking, or use 2 drops of bleach (hypochlorite) per liter and wait 30 minutes.
Boat transport: plan your trips, because the river is going down and rocks and sandbanks appear.
Fishing: with the river low, fish gather together; follow the local fishing rules.
Fire: do not burn trash or fields, because in dry weather fire spreads fast.
acoes.SECA.ALERTA: Drinking water: save it and use it first for drinking and cooking.
Only drink boiled, filtered or hypochlorite-treated water.
Boat transport: before traveling, ask about the stretch and take extra water, food and fuel.
Fishing and food: store food and medicines, because supplies by boat may be delayed.
Fire and smoke: do not burn anything and protect children and elderly people from smoke.
acoes.SECA.EMERGENCIA: Drinking water: go to Civil Defense to receive water and food.
Do not drink untreated river water: with the river very low, diseases increase.
Boat transport: avoid trips that are not urgent.
Fire: if you see fire, call 193 (Fire Department).
Health: in case of diarrhea or fever, go to the health post or call 192.
mochila: Flashlight and batteries, or a charged phone
Phone numbers: 199 Civil Defense, 193 Fire Department, 192 Ambulance (SAMU)
ra.cotas.cheia.PROVISORIA: Flood (provisional levels): there is no official SGB/SACE level for this station (searched in 11/2026). Calculated from the largest flood of each year recorded by ANA from {ini} to {fim} ({anos} years): Watch = the flood passes this level in 1 of every 2 years; Alert = in 1 of every 3 years; Emergency = in 1 of every 10 years.
ra.cotas.seca.PROVISORIA: Drought (provisional levels): calculated from the lowest levels of each year (ANA, {ini}–{fim}): Watch = the river stays below this level in 1 of every 2 years; Alert = in 1 of every 3 years; Emergency = in 1 of every 10 years. It also counts as drought when the river is among the lowest 25% (Watch), 10% (Alert) or 5% (Emergency) of levels for the time of year.

ajuda.intro: Tell Civil Defense how you are. It works even without internet: the request is saved on the phone and sent automatically when the connection comes back.
ajuda.estouBem.explica: Lets them know you and your family are safe.
ajuda.precisoAjuda.explica: Civil Defense sees your request on the panel and on the map.
ajuda.detalhes: Tell us a bit more (if you can)
ajuda.localizacao.explica: Helps the team reach you. The phone may ask for permission.
ajuda.enviado: Received {quando}. Civil Defense will see it on the panel.
ajuda.estouBem.enviado: Thank you! We let them know you are OK ({quando}).
ajuda.guardado: No internet right now: the request was saved on this phone and will be sent automatically when the connection comes back.
ajuda.erro: It was not possible to send. Check the information and try again.
ajuda.limite: Too many requests in a short time. If it is urgent, call 193 or 199.
ajuda.semLocalizacao: We could not get your location. The request goes without it.
ajuda.urgente: If it is urgent, call now
ajuda.whatsapp.explica: Opens WhatsApp with the message ready, so you choose who to send it to.
ajuda.whatsapp.texto: I need help in {lugar}. We are {n} person(s).
ajuda.ouvir: I need help. Tap I am OK to say you are safe, or I need help to call Civil Defense. If it is urgent, call 193 for the Fire Department or 199 for Civil Defense.
painel.entrar.explica: Civil Defense area. Type the panel password.
painel.entrar.BLOQUEADO: Too many wrong attempts. Wait 15 minutes.
painel.entrar.PAINEL_TRANCADO: Panel locked: set the PAINEL_SENHA variable on the server and restart it.
painel.sensor.simulado: SIMULATED: accelerated time, each reading counts as 1 hour.
painel.manual.explica: Sends a warning written by Civil Defense through the channels that are on. It does not change the level calculated by the system.
painel.manual.enviado: Alert sent through the channels that are on.
estacao.14330000.localizacao: on the Rio Negro, about 33 km downstream from the city
ajuda.privacidade: What for: only so Civil Defense knows who needs help and where.
Who sees it: only the Civil Defense team, on the password-protected panel. We do not sell or share it.
For how long: requests are deleted automatically after {dias} days.
Everything is optional: name, phone and location. You can ask for help without them.
Why we can use it: to protect life (Brazil's LGPD, art. 7, VII). To ask for your data to be deleted, talk to Civil Defense.
painel.limpar.pedidos: Also delete all help requests and replies (only to prepare the presentation)
conexao.sem: No internet connection. This screen keeps working with what is saved on this phone.

instalar.explica: AvisaBrasil stays on your phone screen like an app and opens even without internet (Home and I need help), with the last saved data.
